newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IG Metall boss pledges EMU support.
newsitem.headline: German IG Metall boss pledges EMU support.

text.p: The head of Germany's most powerful trade union, IG Metall, said on Wednesday his organisation backed European monetary union as a necessary counter-balance to economic globalisation.

Speaking at a meeting of Frankfurt freemasons, Klaus Zwickel said the impact of deregulation and the removal of trade barriers on labour markets had to be kept in check by increased political cooperation across national borders.

"A closer European Union could create a European social model uniting not only the principle of free competition with welfare provision, but also a regulated market economy with social democracy," he said in a text of the speech released ahead of delivery.

Zwickel, whose union has 2.7 million members in Germany's huge metal and engineering industries, repeated calls for the currency union, due to start in 1999, to be accompanied by specific employment and social provisions.

Union leaders around Europe, including Zwickel, have repeatedly pointed to a requirement in the Maastricht Treaty on currency union that participating states promote a "high level" of employment and social protection.

They insist that the fiscal criteria laid out for the single currency, which have led a number of governments to embark on deeply unpopular austerity programmes, are not binding and should be interpreted flexibly.
But neither the unions nor Europe's political left have so far managed to have additional clauses, such as binding upper thresholds on unemployment, included in the Maastricht Treaty.
The EU summit in Amsterdam this June is likely to be their last chance before membership in the currency union is determined in early 1998.
